messages:
Jordan Lee: Quick Q — ACME's security questionnaire wants: 1) canonical subprocessors list, 2) confirmation on whether logs contain PII, and 3) whether we ever share customer KMS keys. Can we do a quick async check and lock down a short answer by EOD?
Maria Chen: I can assemble the subproc list (S3, Datadog, Fastly, Segment-lite). Will run it past legal but can share a vetted list.
Owen Patel: Logs — app request logs only contain hashed user ids + truncated request ids. Dev exception traces sometimes include raw input (rare). We should say "no PII in production logs; dev traces are redacted by default" if we have a remediation note.
Zia Rahman: KMS — we never share customer KMS keys. For hosted customers we use envelope encryption with service CMK in our KMS; for Private deployments customers can bring their own KMS. Short answer: "we do not share keys; BYOK available for Private".
Alex Gomez: Who signs off on the final wording for the customer doc? Legal or Sec? Also ACME asked if subprocessors have access to customer data — we should indicate access scopes.
Maria Chen: For access: only the vendor accounts with explicit roles can access logs (readonly ops or SRE emergencies). I'll add a one-line access control statement. Legal will OK the subproc list export; Sec team can approve the access wording.
Jordan Lee: Cool. Draft sentence I propose to send: ```We maintain a list of subprocessors (attached). Production logs do not contain PII; dev traces are redacted in prod and access is limited. We do not share customer KMS keys; BYOK is supported for Private deployments.``` Thoughts?
Owen Patel: looks good. Add a note: "exception traces are automatically redacted and retained for 7 days by default" — customers sometimes ask retention windows.
Zia Rahman: +1. Also add: "subprocessors have contractually-limited access and undergo security reviews" — simple statement.
Maria Chen: I'll attach the subproc CSV and a short table of retention/roles. pinging @sec-bot for checklist: do we need any extra wording for SOC2/ISO? :thumbsup:
sec-bot: Checklist: 1) Subprocessors list (CSV) — required. 2) Logging statement — include retention & redaction — recommended. 3) KMS statement — required. 4) Legal signature on list — required. 5) Link to SOC2 summary — optional. See https://internal.redwood/security/controls.
Alex Gomez: Thanks — once legal signs, I can send the response to ACME. Anyone object to the draft?
Jordan Lee: No objections. Maria can you drop the CSV and the final one-paragraph answer in this thread when ready? Aim to send by 5pm PT.
Maria Chen: Will do — uploading CSV and final text in ~2h.
Owen Patel: Small follow-up: for the logging statement let's include the regex we use for email redaction in case they ask technical detail: ```sed -E 's/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}//g'```
Zia Rahman: Noted. Also prepared a short KMS diagram (private link) if ACME wants architecture.
Jordan Lee: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
